what_worked: Strong central thesis about concentration; the 44× mean/median contrast and followers-vs-subscribers comparison land well.
fix_next: AI revenue figures are wildly inflated (~8× the reference); verify every number against the actual dataset before presenting claims as fact.
verdict: Compelling narrative undermined by several fabricated-looking revenue figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: Average stated as $133,750; actual total $15.6M/1000 ≈ $15,596, off by ~8.6×. The 44× ratio and $3,068 median may follow from the inflated mean. Slide 4: Top-10 share stated 50.6% vs reference 49.6%—minor but the largest company figure $25M and 18.7% share are unverifiable and suspicious given total revenue is only $15.6M (that single company would exceed total). Slide 5: 109 companies earned zero vs reference 216—roughly half the correct count. Slide 9: AI total revenue stated $18,428,213 vs reference $2,356,676—inflated ~7.8×. AI median stated $4,301 vs reference $503—inflated ~8.5×. E-commerce revenue stated $12,018,508 vs reference $1,111,606—inflated ~10.8×. These appear to be annualized (×12) from 30-day figures without disclosure, but even then the multiplier doesn't consistently match.

evidence.insight: Slide 8's juxtaposition of 205× MRR gap vs 6× follower gap is a genuinely useful insight. Slide 9's 'crowded ≠ profitable' framing adds value. The B2B/B2C flip (slide 7) is a strong analytical move.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: establish skew (slides 3-5) → ask what winners do differently (slide 6) → three answers (slides 7-9) → geography/exits (10-11) → synthesis (12). The title 'The Thousand and the Ten' anchors everything. Closing line is memorable.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 sets up the dataset but never mentions missingness (241 country, 288 audience_type, 274 category missing). No source attribution. No time period specified for revenue. The audience is implied (founders) but never stated. '29 data points' is stated but columns aren't enumerated.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple revenue figures appear inflated by roughly 8-12× (possibly annualizing 30-day data without stating so, but even then inconsistent). Zero-revenue count (109 vs 216) is materially wrong. The single largest company earning $25M would exceed the entire dataset's total revenue of $15.6M—a logical impossibility that wasn't caught. Top-10 share 50.6% vs 49.6% is minor.
evidence.visual: Gamma template provides consistent styling. Charts are simple and readable. Slide 4's bar chart has a mislabel ('Total conversion rate'). Decorative AI-generated illustrations on slides 1, 2, 6, 10 add atmosphere but no information. Slide 3's comparison chart is effective. Slide 11's bar chart comparing $86.8M to $35K is a poor use of a bar chart (scale makes median invisible).
evidence.ai_slop: Gamma watermark visible. Decorative illustrations on 4 slides are AI-generated and content-free. Slide 4 has a spurious 'Total conversion rate' label—likely a template artifact. The illustrations (storefront, forking road, globe) are thematic but generic.
